analyst_view.overall: Braga (17th, 4 pts) host KuPS (33rd, 1 pt) and need the win to move toward the top 24; Braga are unbeaten in four under Franclim Carvalho, who replaced Carlos Vicens in October, including a 2-0 cup win at Vitoria de Guimaraes on Saturday, and have won 14 of their last 16 home European games. Braga are without Sikou Niakate (Achilles), whom the numbers already list, and striker Jonas Wind is doubtful with physical overload, which they don't count; Navarro, Horta and Pau Victor should start and Gabriel Silva may return. KuPS finished third in Finland and their season ended weeks ago, so they arrive rusty after seven games without a win, with two goals in three European games; winger Bob Nii Armah is doubtful (counted). Ukrainian referee Oleksiy Derevinskyi is named, and the numbers already trim cards a little for his record.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals, about 2.1 of them Braga's. I lean a little higher: KuPS' league season is over and they arrive after weeks without a competitive match and seven games without a win, which the numbers can't see, while Braga's attack is scoring again under Franclim even without Wind. A mild +4% gives about 2.7 goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, about 7 for Braga, already lifted 9% for Braga's recent corner count and cut for KuPS' few. KuPS will mostly defend deep, which the split already reflects, so I stay at about 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, already trimmed for both sides' quiet recent discipline and for referee Derevinskyi's low card count (-3%). A one-sided game against a team defending deep usually stays calm, which is what the numbers show, so I stay at about 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.7 shots, already pushed up 26% for Braga's recent shot volume and down 13% for KuPS'. KuPS' rustiness argues for even more Braga pressure, but Braga played a cup tie on Saturday and may rotate, and the numbers already carry a big lift, so I stay at about 29.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target, 7.5 of them Braga's. A KuPS side out of season should give up cleaner chances than usual, which the numbers can't see, and Navarro's return to scoring helps Braga's finishing, so I lean slightly higher: +3% gives about 10.4.
